knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CH-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines the moment generating function and cumulant generating function of X?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The MGF is E[exp(tX)], and its logarithm is the CGF.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: M_X(t)=E[e^(tX)] and K_X(t)=log M_X(t), where the MGF exists.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Confusing the MGF with a distribution function or the CGF transformation.

choices.label: M_X(t) = E[exp(tX)] where finite, and K_X(t) = log M_X(t).
M_X(t) = E[tX], and K_X(t) is its derivative.
M_X(t) = P(X less than or equal to t), and K_X(t) is the survival function.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: CH-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. If the MGF of X exists around zero, how are its first two raw moments obtained?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The nth MGF derivative at zero gives the nth raw moment; variance subtracts the squared mean.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Calling the second raw moment the variance.

choices.label: E[X] = M_X'(0) and E[X squared] = M_X''(0).
E[X] = M_X(0) and E[X squared] = M_X'(0).
